claim: For full n-copy density reconstruction of rho_(r,v)=(I+r v.sigma)/2 over v in S^2, known c0<=r*sqrt(n)<=c1 and sufficiently large n, no reference/assistance, and maximum quantum branch dimension Q with classical labels charged separately, Q_min=Theta(r/epsilon) for r^2<=epsilon<=r and Q_min=Theta(min{n+1,sqrt(n[1+log(r^2/epsilon)])}) for 0<epsilon<r^2, with constants depending only on c0,c1.
supplied_inputs: n, r, compact critical-radius constants c0,c1, and target epsilon; v is unknown.
acquired_inputs: No direction is acquired. The lower permits arbitrary classical outcome spaces and sector-changing decoders; the upper uses a finite O(n^3)-label design.
costs: Maximum branch dimension Q; upper total direct-sum dimension O(n^3 Q), with the O(n^3) finite labels charged. Schur transforms, exact quadrature synthesis, circuit runtime, finite gate precision, and physical output preparation are separate costs. No minimum total-D claim follows.
proof: New tail lower uses exact large-spin derivatives, a per-Kraus score deficit 1/(786432*r*Q^3) for every output sector, a parity-resolved Schur band lower mass, and a score-width conversion. Upper uses the tapered rank-Q channel and an explicit Rademacher tail moment bound. Endpoint inversion joins the fixed-Q regime and exact Q=n+1 recovery.
evidence: Analytic audit records in outputs/research/combinatorics_optimization/cycle3/tail_audit/{derivative,score,spin_band,tail_upper,endpoints,tail_upper_spectral}.txt. Exact integer Schur-band replay passed two rational fixtures in work/programmes/combinatorics_optimization/cycle3/tail_audit/check_exact_band.py; finite evidence is not proof.
falsifier: A failure of the derivative bounds, an output-sector Kraus with smaller score deficit, a parity/Stirling band-mass violation, a score-to-trace normalization error, or a legal code beating the lower bound.
scope_caveat: For the unknown-radius ball of radius c1/sqrt(n), exact transitions are c1^2/n and c1/sqrt(n); if the full epsilon range reaches c1/sqrt(n) with c1>1, state the omitted constant-Q interval above n^(-1/2) or restrict the range.
